name: The Connaught
positioning: Historic Mayfair hotel on Carlos Place, first opened in 1815 and renamed The Connaught in 1917, with a large private art collection and the Aman Spa
best_for: Travelers who want a Mayfair base close to Berkeley Square and Mount Street
Guests who want a suite with a personal butler

facts.text: The Connaught is in the heart of Mayfair Village, on the corner of Carlos Place just off Berkeley Square.
The hotel is rooted in its Mount Street neighbourhood.
The hotel started life in 1815 as The Prince of Saxe-Coburg Hotel.
In 1917 it was renamed The Connaught, after Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn.
The reception hall has a gold-leaf-gilded mahogany staircase.
A water installation by Tadao Ando stands outside the front door.
Rooms, designed by Guy Oliver, are split between the original building and the 2007 Connaught Wing.
Bathrooms are in white marble with heated Toto seats.
The Coburg Suites have views over Carlos Place.
The Apartment is a rooftop suite by David Collins Studio.
The Aman Spa is deep within the hotel, and its treatments include a Ku Nye full-body massage inspired by ancient Tibetan healing traditions.
The Connaught Bar, designed by David Collins Studio, is known for its Martini trolley.

highlights.text: A private art collection of more than 3,000 pieces lines the staircase and public spaces.
The subterranean levels hold a black granite pool and a meditative waterfall wall.
Suites come with personal butlers and bespoke experiences.
The King's Lodge suite was created by craftspeople and artisans from The Turquoise Mountain School in Kabul.
The Mews is a three-floor private townhouse with an outside terrace and a baby grand.

considerations.text: The pool and spa are on the hotel's subterranean levels.
Accessible rooms are in both the new and old parts of the building, with ramp access via The Connaught Bar.
WhataHotel notes a traditional, formal atmosphere that may not suit all travelers.
